title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to the unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche, 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. Section 8° on the previous page returns to the 'universal case', indexed by 0. The base group is presumably the profinite completion of SL(2,Z), or the corresponding cartographic or Teichmüller group for type (1,1). rho and sigma are the standard generators of order 3 and 2. 𝔊_0^+ and 𝔊_0^ς are subgroups, presumably finite-index or level-type. M is a group or monoid of 'GT-type' automorphisms. The conditions in (107) define M^ς: an element u must send rho, sigma and epsilon_0 to 𝔊^ς-conjugates of prescribed powers, governed by a character chi(u) = mu, and must stabilise 𝔊^ς. The page records the following structure.

(108) The 'centraliser-like' group Z_{rho_0,sigma_0} embeds into M[0]. Here M[0] = M(0)·L_0^𝔊 (a product of a 'pure' part M(0) with inner automorphisms L_0^𝔊). M[0] is isomorphic to the analogous genus-0, three-point object M̃_{0,3}[0] = M̃_{0,3}(0)·L_0^{𝔊_{0,3}}. The embedding is an equality when 𝔊_0^ς = 𝔊_0^+. In the extreme case where 𝔊_0^ς = Π or Π_0, it identifies Z with M^![0] ≅ M(0)·L_0^Π.

In a bracketed aside, Grothendieck makes this explicit when 𝔊_0^ς ⊂ Π_0, giving (109). Z_{rho,sigma} consists of the products u = u_0·ℓ, with u_0 ∈ M(0) and ℓ an inner automorphism by Π, satisfying three conditions:
(a) u acts on rho as an inner automorphism alpha;
(b) u acts on sigma as an inner automorphism beta, with alpha, beta in the relevant centraliser-type subgroup 𝔊_c^ς;
(c) u stabilises 𝔊_0^ς.
He notes that alpha and beta are uniquely determined by u. They range over a group isomorphic to a product of the form Aut(𝔊_0^+) × Ẑ' × μ × μ (reference to p. 629). Using the group laws, the assignment is compatible with the maps to M̃_{0,3}[0] and hence to M[0]^! ≅ M̃_{0,3}[0].

A margin note judges this explicitation 'useless' ('ne semble servir à rien'). The next page uses (108) to define a morphism of 'systems' (110)→(111): group, normal subgroup, action, embedding. By the construction of 9°, this yields a morphism of the associated extension groups G_{rho_0,sigma_0} → M.

Mathematically, the page is a bookkeeping step. It compares automorphisms of the genus-1 (type (1,1)) profinite group that preserve conjugacy classes of the torsion generators with GT-type automorphisms of the genus-0 three-point group (the free profinite group on two generators).
errors: No outright error is detectable. The identification and the inclusion conditions depend on definitions from pp. 629 ff. that are not visible here.
The product decomposition of the group of (alpha, beta) data is only partly legible, so it cannot be checked.

ideas.what: Embedding the group of automorphisms of the (1,1)-type profinite group that preserve the conjugacy classes of rho and sigma into the GT-type automorphism group of the (0,3) group, with equality in the full level
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of GT actions on Γ̂_{1,1} (or SL2(Z)^ / B̂_3) and on F̂_2 = π_1(M_{0,4}); the genus-1 version of GT
ideas.where_published: Only foreshadowed in Esquisse d'un programme (the 'Lego' with Ĝ_{0,4}, Ĝ_{1,1}); the details are unpublished

ideas.what: Explicit description (109) of Z as products u_0·ℓ (pure part times inner automorphism) acting on rho and sigma by uniquely determined inner automorphisms alpha and beta
ideas.modern_name: Normalised GT elements modulo inner automorphisms; uniqueness of the conjugating elements because of trivial centralisers

ideas.what: Building a morphism of extension data (group, subgroup, action, embedding) to obtain a canonical homomorphism between the induced groups (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of the pushout/extension construction for outer actions

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical intermediate step comparing genus-1 and genus-0 GT-type automorphism groups. The same comparison was later developed in the literature by Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps and others. Grothendieck himself marks the explicit part as useless, and nothing new beyond bookkeeping is visible.
transcription_corrections: The script letter is 𝔊 (as on the neighbouring pages), not 𝔖: read L_0^𝔊, 𝔊_0^ς, 𝔊_0^+, L_0^{𝔊_{0,3}}.
In (108) read Z_{ρ_0,σ_0} (the subscript 0 appears under ρ as well as on σ).
The first line likely reads 'On a un groupe … = M(0).L_0^𝔊,' with M[0] placed above the arrow.
(109): the right-hand side is 'u = u_0.ℓ, with u_0 ∈ M(0), ℓ ∈ L_0^Π'. Condition (c) reads 'u stabilise 𝔊_0^ς', and α, β ∈ 𝔊_c^ς.
The bracket opens with '— en fait, si 𝔊_0^ς ⊂ Π_0, alors on trouve'.
